title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Dow Hangs Ten Above 50,000 While Tech Wipes Out
conditions.summary: The Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time as money rotated into health care and staples, while a chip-stock pullback dragged the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lower.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Dow +423 pts (+0.85%) to 50,018.70, its first close above 50,000.
Chip stocks gave back part of Monday's Nvidia-led rally; the S&P opened lower, was down about 1% at midday, and trimmed losses late.
Health care (+2.2%) and consumer staples (+1.8%) led; technology (-3.7%) was the worst sector, with 8 of 11 sectors higher.
Breadth was positive even as heavyweight tech pulled the cap-weighted indexes down.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 in November from 91.9, far above the roughly 92.5 consensus and the highest since January 2025.
Case-Shiller 20-city prices rose 0.1% in September (0.2% expected); FHFA prices were flat (0.2% expected); Richmond Fed manufacturing improved to +3.
Reports that the US is preparing higher tariffs on China and dozens of other countries weighed on futures early.
No Fed speakers today; money markets are pricing a December rate hike after NY Fed President Williams warned Monday that sticky inflation points to tighter policy.
10-year yield eased about 1 bp to 4.90%; WTI crude rose to about $82; gold fell about 2.7%; bitcoin dipped below $60,000; VIX near 26. Dollar index was about 104.2 in morning trade.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: INSM (Insmed): +14.1% — Sanofi agreed to buy it for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion.
ANF (Abercrombie & Fitch): +19.7% — strong quarter and a raised full-year profit outlook.
KSS (Kohl's): +19.5% — sales beat and a raised outlook.
DKS (Dick's Sporting Goods): +14.6% — big earnings beat and a higher full-year forecast.
DLTR (Dollar Tree): +11.2% — revenue up 6.9% and a raised profit outlook.
ADI (Analog Devices): -17.4% — fell despite a record quarter and solid guidance.
HPE (Hewlett Packard Enterprise): -16.3% — margin warning overshadowed strong revenue guidance.
MU (Micron): -11.0%; AMD: -8.9%; NVDA (Nvidia): -5.9% — chips gave back Monday's surge.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: Best Buy beat with comps +6.1% and rose 2.7%; Burlington rose 3.9% despite soft Q4 guidance; Medtronic narrowly beat on profit but missed on revenue.
Retail winners Abercrombie, Kohl's, Dick's and Dollar Tree all rallied on beats and raised outlooks.
After the close: Dell posted revenue of $54.9B versus about $50.6B expected and adjusted EPS of $9.45, and raised its full-year revenue forecast to $202B.
Dell shares rose roughly 2% to 3% after hours following a 12% drop in the regular session.
HP, Autodesk, Workday, Nutanix and Urban Outfitters also reported after the bell.

sections.title: Business News
items: Sanofi's roughly $41 billion cash deal for Insmed is expected to close in the first half of 2027.
Anthropic shares fell about 6.5% and closed below their $83 IPO price.
Stripe's valuation is reportedly set to top $200 billion in a tender offer.
Tesla and SpaceX reportedly formed special board committees to study an all-stock combination.
The Pentagon is reportedly in talks with GM and Ford about mass-producing drones.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: October PCE inflation (core expected +0.3% m/m, 3.4% y/y), personal income and spending, Q3 GDP second estimate (about 3.5% expected), jobless claims and durable goods.
9:00 AM CT: October new home sales.
1:00 PM CT: Fed Beige Book; no Fed speakers scheduled.
Earnings: Deere before the open.
Markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving; Friday closes early at 12:00 PM CT.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down behind the water, the last set is rolling in, and it was a split day out there. Tariff headlines and Fed hike worries hung over the lineup. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sandpipers and he is still wired. Say good evening to the crew, Gus! Let's start with the final set. The Dow climbed four hundred twenty-three points, or about eight tenths of a percent, to fifty thousand eighteen. That's the first close ever above fifty thousand. Cowabunga, that's a big wave, and it's worth a biscuit. Here you go, buddy! But the tech crowd wiped out. The S and P five hundred slipped half a percent to seven thousand two hundred one. The Nasdaq fell about one and a half percent to twenty-three thousand seven hundred thirty-four. Small caps did fine, with the Russell two thousand up about six tenths of a percent. The story was rotation. After Monday's monster Nvidia rally on Jensen Huang's return, chip stocks gave a lot of it back. Tech was the worst sector, down close to four percent, while health care and consumer staples led. Most stocks actually rose. Now the wind and weather. Consumer confidence came in gnarly strong, jumping to one hundred three point three from about ninety-two, way above forecasts and the best reading since early twenty twenty-five. The ten year Treasury yield eased about one basis point to four point nine percent. Crude oil jumped more than two percent to about eighty-two dollars. Gold dropped nearly three percent, bitcoin slid under sixty thousand dollars, and the VIX fear gauge held near twenty-six. Over in the lineup, Insmed popped fourteen percent after Sanofi agreed to buy it for about forty-one billion dollars in cash. Abercrombie and Fitch and Kohl's both surged nearly twenty percent on strong quarters and raised outlooks. Dick's Sporting Goods gained almost fifteen percent and Dollar Tree added eleven. On the wipeout side, Analog Devices sank seventeen percent even after a record quarter. Hewlett Packard Enterprise dropped sixteen percent on a margin warning. And our newest grom, Anthropic, slipped below its I P O price. On the tide chart tonight, Dell crushed estimates after the bell and raised its outlook. The stock rose a few percent after hours, after dropping about twelve percent during the day. In beach talk, Stripe is reportedly heading for a valuation above two hundred billion dollars. Tesla and SpaceX have reportedly formed board committees to look at combining. Now wax your board for tomorrow. At seven thirty A M Central we get a big set: the P C E inflation report, personal income and spending, the second look at third quarter G D P, jobless claims, and durable goods. New home sales follow at nine A M Central, and the Fed's Beige Book lands at one P M Central. Deere reports before the open. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday closes early at noon Central. Catch me on the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. Want me to call a wave for you? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will read the surf for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
